correctness.rationale: Exact stationary balance identity and independent pairwise matrix Bernstein with \(O(n)\) variance yield \(O_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{n\log n})\) operator control. Remainder Euclidean norm is \(O_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{\log n}/n^{3/2})\), so exchangeability kills each fixed-coordinate scaled error; independent external-edge sums give the joint Gaussian law. Shared-edge covariance of squared imbalance is \(\operatorname{Var}((X-X^{\prime})^2)=O(1)\), proving the global \(L^2\) law. The original standalone program directly checked 96 stationary systems, residuals and exact perturbation relations. No finite test was used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The principal 2026 source proves uniform leading occupation and plots qualitative edge-disorder effects but does not state the precise joint scaled Gaussian, empirical Gaussian law, or exact global susceptibility. The 2025 i.i.d. theorem and the 2014 random-generator invariant-measure theorem give first-order convergence bounds. Statement-level comparisons with relevant primary literature did not find a stronger covering theorem. Risk remains of an unlocated general stationary-eigenvector CLT.
residual_risks: A potentially broader random stationary-eigenvector CLT might imply the second-order laws and was not located or exhaustively excluded.
The 2008 circular-law paper was inspected at abstract level only and is not used as whole-text negative evidence.
The theorem assumes bounded positive exchangeable edge pairs; unbounded heavy-tailed generalizations remain unproved.

value.rationale: Calvert 2026 motivates why large dense nonequilibrium networks can look equilibrium-like in static occupation; an exact and measurable next-order diagnostic is needed. The local Gaussian law and global susceptibility identify only antisymmetric edge-current disorder. Three distinct edge-pair couplings with identical one-edge marginals have exact limiting susceptibility 0, 1/2 and 1, distinguishing balance, uncorrelated nonequilibrium and maximally anticorrelated disorder. This is a structural second-order classification, not merely a numerical invariant or restatement of uniformity.
